subject: RFP: SLA measurement boundary conditions & sampling proposal
messages:
From: Susan Meyer <susan.meyer@horizonfin.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dan Cho <dan.cho@horizonfin.com>, procurement@horizonfin.com
Date: 2027-01-11T08:12:00Z
Subject: RFP: SLA measurement clarifications — latency windows & sampling

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the quick look at our RFP. A few follow-ups from the technical evaluation team around how Redwood intends to measure uptime and latency for the purposes of SLA credits:

1) Measurement window: Is availability calculated over calendar-month wall-clock time, or over a rolling 30-day window? We need clarity because our accounting runs on monthly invoices.
2) Sampling vs continuous: Do you measure every request in production telemetry, or will you provide a sampled latency dataset? If sampled, what sampling rate and stratification (by region, model, route) do you apply?
3) Cache warm-up and cold-starts: For models with large KV caches, how are warm-up latency spikes treated in the measurement window (ignored, excluded, or included)?
4) Multi-region failover: If traffic is routed to a secondary region during an outage, is that considered degraded service or equivalent availability? How are cross-region routing latencies accounted for?
5) Evidence package: For invoking credits we need raw traces, HTTP request/response samples (headers + timing), and the telemetry query used to compute the aggregate metric.

We attached a short list of the RFP questions (Horizon-RFP-SLA-questions.pdf) for your reference. Can you provide a proposed measurement and sampling approach by COB tomorrow?

Regards,
Susan
Procurement & IT Risk
Horizon Financial

Attachments: Horizon-RFP-SLA-questions.pdf (pdf, 48KB)
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Susan Meyer <susan.meyer@horizonfin.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-01-11T13:40:00Z
Subject: Re: RFP: SLA measurement clarifications — latency windows & sampling

Hi Susan — thanks for these clear questions and for the RFP appendix. High level answers up front and a short proposal attached (SLA-measurement-proposal.xlsx). We can walk Horizon through the details on a call; proposing Wed 14th.

Summary answers:
- Measurement window: Default is calendar-month for invoicing, with an optional rolling 30-day view for operational debugging. Credits are computed on calendar-month granularity unless otherwise negotiated.
- Sampling vs continuous: We continuously ingest telemetry for all production requests. For SLA computation we run production-grade aggregations on the full telemetry set; we also provide stratified sampled exports for long-term storage to limit bandwidth for customers who request raw rows.
- Warm-up/cold-starts: Our baseline is to include all production requests. However, we exclude trace-level outliers tied to node provisioning events (autoscaling events that we can correlate) in the first 10 minutes after a cold pool spin-up; this is documented and auditable.
- Multi-region failover: Failover to a warmed secondary region counts as served (availability) but we mark the window as degraded for latency-tier calculations if 95th/99th p95/p99 exceed your thresholds. Service credits calculation uses the higher-severity classification.
- Evidence package: We can produce a zip with raw trace extracts (anonymized IPs), the telemetry queries, and a sampling manifest. We retain 90 days by default for trace exports and 365 days for aggregated metrics, with enterprise retention available.

Please see the attached spreadsheet for the proposed sampling schema, query examples, and our suggested credit table. Marcus and Laura can add technical and legal nuance.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SLA-measurement-proposal.xlsx (xlsx, 120KB)

Subject: Re: RFP: SLA measurement clarifications — latency windows & sampling

Hi Priya — thanks for the clear summary. A couple of follow-ups after I reviewed the spreadsheet:

- Calendar-month granularity is fine for credits, but Horizon also requires a 30-day rolling SLA widget in-dashboard so our SREs can correlate incidents. Can you confirm you can expose both views?
- On the cold-start exclusion: please clarify what constitutes correlation to an autoscaling event. If there are short-lived cache thrash incidents (example: sudden cache invalidation due to model redeploy), will those be excluded automatically? We need exclusions to be reproducible and queryable.
- For multi-region: if traffic is routed from us-east-1 to us-west-2 and the client sees >50ms additional median latency because of cross-region hop, will that be considered a failure or a degradation? Horizon's policy treats cross-region routing as degraded, not a full outage.

Also attached is a short network diagram we use for vendors (region-failover-diagram.png).

Would welcome a short note from Marcus on the cold-start/caching logic and from your SRE on how you detect/prove autoscale-related latency spikes.

Thanks,
Susan
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Susan Meyer <susan.meyer@horizonfin.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: RFP: SLA measurement clarifications — latency windows & sampling

Hi team — quick technical note to clarify how we operationalize exclusions and detect autoscaling-related events: 

1) Autoscale correlation: every scaling event (scale-out or scale-in) is recorded in the control plane with timestamps and affected instance ids. Our telemetry pipeline annotates request traces that land on those instance ids. Exclusions are implemented by a reproducible query that filters out requests where request.timestamp is within [scale_event_start, scale_event_end + 10 minutes] and the trace.annotation contains "node:provisioned".

2) Cache invalidation vs redeploy: We treat planned model redeploys (triggered by a rollout) as a separate event type and annotate them. Unplanned cache thrash (e.g., a sudden spike in unique prefixes leading to eviction storms) is detected by a combination of cache miss-rate delta (>30% over baseline) and observed tail latency spike correlated across the node pool. Those are not excluded automatically; they are considered part of production behavior unless the customer requests an incident review and we find an infrastructure cause (e.g., buggy orchestration causing cascading restarts).

3) Sampling and stratification: For raw export we provide a stratified sample at 1% overall, but 100% for requests that hit p95/p99 thresholds (we flag tail requests and keep them). For SLA computation we use full-aggregation, not sampling.

4) Cross-region routing: We classify cross-region served traffic as 'available but degraded'. For credits we compute two metrics per window: availability (served vs failed) and latency-tier breach (percent of requests exceeding threshold). Credits are applied based on the worst of the two. So if cross-region serving keeps availability at 100% but causes p99 to exceed the contract threshold for >5% of minutes in the month, that will trigger the corresponding credit tier.

Happy to provide the exact SQL query and a sample dataset; attaching a one-pager in our internal follow-up.

—Marcus
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-01-13T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: RFP: SLA measurement boundary conditions & sampling proposal — next steps

Susan / Dan — thanks for the quick turn. We're aligned on the high-level approach and the principles Marcus outlined. Action items and agreed points below: 

- Redwood will include both calendar-month credit calculations and a 30-day rolling dashboard view for Horizon SREs (deliverable: dashboard link + readme).
- Exclusions: autoscale provisioning windows will be excluded by default for the 10-minute post-provision buffer using the reproducible query Marcus mentioned. Planned redeploys will be annotated but included in metrics; unplanned cache thrash remains included unless an infrastructure cause is proven.
- Cross-region failover: categorized as "available but degraded"; credits compute using worst-case between availability and latency-tier breaches. We will draft precise credit triggers in the SOW.
- Evidence: Redwood will deliver an evidence package on request that includes: anonymized traces, the exact telemetry query, and a manifest. Standard retention: 90 days (traces), 365 days (aggregates); enterprise retention is available per SOW.

Next steps: we will post the draft SOW and the telemetry SQL examples to the shared Drive by EOD Friday (link included). Can we schedule a 45-minute technical review on Thursday 14:00 PST? If that works we'll send calendar invite.

Thanks — Priya
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
